name: Mabuterol
lead: Mabuterol is a selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist developed as an oral bronchodilator for asthma, chemically related to clenbuterol [1][2]. In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding discussion it is grouped with clenbuterol-type compounds that people associate with fat loss and a leaner, more defined physique.

Published human research dates from the 1980s and 1990 and concerns asthma, not body composition. A dose-finding study in 245 asthmatic patients identified 50 micrograms as the optimal single dose, and a 6-week comparison supported 50 micrograms twice daily [2]. A small crossover trial compared it with clenbuterol and fenoterol on early-morning breathing dips [3].
It is not a mainstream marketed drug. Mabuterol appears mostly in analytical chemistry papers that screen for beta-agonist residues in livestock and feed [4].

angle.text: Users group mabuterol with clenbuterol-like compounds sought for cutting body fat. Human studies of it concern asthma, and none have examined fat loss.

card.summary: A clenbuterol-like beta-2 agonist bronchodilator that is discussed as an alternative for cutting body fat and getting leaner.
card.note: Beta-agonists can cause palpitations and tremor; no fat-loss studies exist.

quick.overview:
Mabuterol is a beta-2 agonist originally studied as a tablet for asthma. It is a close chemical relative of clenbuterol.

In physique communities it is mentioned as a clenbuterol-type compound for cutting. It is rarely seen on the market and mostly turns up in drug-residue testing literature.
quick.mechanism: It activates beta-2 adrenergic receptors, relaxing airway smooth muscle, and in animal work was more potent than isoprenaline and salbutamol at relaxing guinea pig trachea [5]. Beta-agonist class effects in the body include increased heart rate.
quick.risks: Clinical studies reported good tolerability at 40-60 micrograms in asthma patients [1]. Related drugs caused palpitations in a comparison trial [3]. Animal toxicology studies reported irritability and salivation at high doses [6]. It is not an approved product in major markets.

infobox: Not a marketed approved drug in major markets

paras: Mabuterol relaxed isolated guinea pig tracheal muscle more potently than isoprenaline and salbutamol in laboratory comparisons [5]. A cardiovascular study in animals reported lowered blood pressure and a slight heart-rate rise at low intravenous doses [7]. In rats it showed enantioselective kinetics, with slow absorption and a longer half-life for the R form [8].

An open pilot of 10 patients with reversible obstructive lung disease found a useful bronchodilating effect at 40 and 60 micrograms with good tolerability [1]. A summary of first studies covered 245 asthma patients in dose-finding and a multicenter 6-week comparison [2]. A randomized crossover study in 10 patients with nocturnal asthma compared it with clenbuterol and fenoterol; all three reduced morning dipping in some lung measures [3]. No studies have examined mabuterol for fat loss or body composition.

Acute, subacute and chronic toxicity studies in mice, rats, rabbits and dogs reported dose-dependent irritability and hypersalivation in rats at 10 mg/kg and above, with deaths at the highest dose [6].
Mabuterol is 1-[4-amino-3-chloro-5-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]-2-(tert-butylamino)ethanol, with molar mass about 310.75 g/mol; patents date to the 1970s [9].
It is mentioned alongside clenbuterol-like beta-agonists for cutting. Analytical papers list it among beta-agonists screened for in animal feed and urine [4].

timeline.event: A series of pharmacology, toxicology and first clinical studies of mabuterol is published [1][2][5][6].
A crossover trial compares mabuterol, clenbuterol and fenoterol in nocturnal asthma [3].
